newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Oil head may resign over deals.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Oil head may resign over deals.

text.p: The chairman of Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd has hinted that he might resign over the firm's involvement in shady oil deals at the centre of a bribery scandal, a Japanese daily reported on Sunday.
"I can't make the decision to resign on my own, but I think it is necessary (for me to step down)," Mitsubishi Oil chairman Kikuo Yamada told the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper.
Yamada came under fire from other Mitsubishi officials over a series of oil product deals with Mitsui Mining Co Ltd that were brokered by millionaire oil wholesaler Junichi Izui, Yomiuri said.
Izui was indicted in November on charges of evading 330 million yen ($2.66 million) in income tax on oil trade commissions between 1992 and 1994.
Izui and two former company executives of Mitsubishi Oil and Mitsui Mining were arrested in January on fraud charges.
Yamada and other officials at Mitsubishi Oil were not immediately available to comment on the report.
